newsitem.title: INDIA: Peregrine maintains India 97/98 deficit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine maintains India 97/98 deficit forecast.

text.p: Peregrine Capital India said on Tuesday it had kept its 1997/98 forecast for India's fiscal deficit as a share of gross domestic product (GDP) at 5.0 percent, despite a lower government estimate.
"The new budget is assuming that the fiscal deficit will hit 4.5 percent of the nominal GDP in the coming year," the securities said in a report released after last week's federal budget.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday the government had set the fiscal deficit target at 4.5 percent of GDP for 1997/98 (April-March). The government's estimate of the 1996/97 fiscal deficit remained at 5.0 percent of GDP, he said while presenting the federal budget.
But Peregrine said it was unlikely that the fiscal deficit could be contained at 5.0 percent during the current year.
"The deficit is estimated by Peregrine to have reached 5.6 percent of GDP in 1996/97," Peregrine said.

"The government claims this is 5.0 percent, but that would have required nominal GDP to have grown by over 25 percent last year. Given that, even by the government's own estimates, real GDP growth is weaker this year than last, it is highly unlikely that a feat of this magnitude could have been achieved," it said.

India expects real GDP to grow at seven percent or more in 1997/98, finance ministry officials said on Saturday. Real GDP is expected to grow at 6.8 percent in 1996/97 against 7.1 in the previous financial year.
"It is difficult to think of any country in the world that has achieved that kind of expansion recently," Peregrine said.
"We stand by our fiscal deficit forecast of 5.0 percent of the GDP in 1997/98."
